draft.title: Financial institutions
card: Financial institutions collect money from savers and investors and supply finance to businesses in different forms. Each type does this in its own way.
Banks
take deposits and lend money to businesses, for example through overdrafts and term loans.
Investment banks
do not mainly lend from deposits. They help large businesses raise finance, for example by arranging share issues, and advise on takeovers.
Finance companies

lend money and offer leasing. They often lend to borrowers that banks turn down, usually at higher interest rates. Superannuation funds, life insurers and unit trusts pool money from many people and invest it, so businesses receive finance when these funds buy their shares or debt.
draft.remember: Each institution supplies finance differently: lending, arranging, leasing or investing pooled money.

a.q: Which institution mainly helps a large company raise finance by arranging a share issue?
a.why: Investment banks help large businesses raise finance, such as by arranging share issues. A finance company lends and leases, so it is the tempting wrong choice, but it does not mainly arrange share issues.
a.clue: Think about which institution does not mainly lend from deposits.

b.q: Kiri runs a small removalist firm in Bathurst. A bank has refused her a loan for a new truck. Which institution is most likely to lend to her, probably at a higher interest rate?
b.why: Finance companies lend and lease, often to borrowers that banks turn down, and they usually charge higher interest. An investment bank is tempting, but it serves large businesses by arranging finance rather than lending to a small firm.
b.clue: Which institution often lends where banks will not?
